evals.prompt: We had an incident yesterday (INC-4117) — someone committed a private key file (*.pem) and we had to rotate half our credentials. Add a governance rule that blocks committing *.pem, *.key, and *.p12 files. Wire it into the constitution properly.
evals.expected_output: Three coordinated artifacts land together in one commit: (a) a new tests/governance/rules/<rule-name>/ rule folder with rule.yaml, check.sh, and constitution.md that blocks committing the listed key/cert extensions, (b) a new Invariants subsection in CONSTITUTION.md describing the rule and citing INC-4117, and (c) an Evolution Log entry with today's date summarizing the amendment. The rule is tested against a seeded repo with and without a .pem file. The skill drafts, smoke-tests, and commits in one pass without asking for approval of the draft. The final summary reports the rule name, action type, smoke-test result, the commit sha+subject, and that the next step is `git push` for PR review.
assertions: A new rule folder was created under tests/governance/rules/ with a name matching the invariant (e.g., no-key-material/check.sh)
The rule check blocks at least these extensions: .pem, .key, .p12
The rule check has a rationale comment naming INC-4117
The rule check uses rule_start, violation, rule_end, and sources lib.sh (consistent with existing conventions)
CONSTITUTION.md gained a new Invariants subsection that names the rule and cites INC-4117
CONSTITUTION.md's Evolution Log gained a new entry dated today describing the amendment
Running tests/governance/run.sh on a repo containing a staged *.pem file produces a violation referencing the new rule
Running tests/governance/run.sh on a clean repo (no key files) exits 0 after the amendment
The skill created exactly one new commit containing all three artifacts with a conventional-commit subject
The skill did not pause to ask the user for approval of the draft before writing or committing
The skill reported the action type, smoke-test result, commit sha+subject, and `git push` next step in its final summary

evals.prompt: We want to raise our file-size-limit from 500 lines to 800 lines — the old limit is triggering too many false positives in the data-pipeline package. Amend the constitution.
evals.expected_output: The existing file-size-limit rule's limit is updated (either directly in check.sh or via the GOVERNANCE_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT env var convention). The constitution's invariant section for file-size-limit is updated to reflect 800. A new Evolution Log entry records the change with a reason (false positives in data-pipeline). No new rule folder is created — this is an amendment to an existing rule, not a new one.
assertions: The existing file-size-limit rule folder was edited (not duplicated)
The new limit value (800) appears in check.sh or its env var default
The CONSTITUTION.md invariant for file-size-limit references 800 (not 500)
A new Evolution Log entry was added with today's date describing the limit change and citing the data-pipeline false-positive reason
No new rule folder was created
The skill created exactly one new commit containing the amendment with a conventional-commit subject
The amendment summary reported that this was an update rather than a new rule

evals.prompt: Remove the no-console-log rule — we're keeping structured logs via pino and the rule is noisy. Do it properly.
evals.expected_output: Three coordinated deletions/edits: the rule folder is removed, the corresponding Invariants subsection is removed from CONSTITUTION.md, and an Evolution Log entry records the removal with a reason (structured logging via pino makes the rule redundant). The skill warns if any other docs or code references the removed rule by name.
assertions: tests/governance/rules/no-console-log no longer exists
The Invariants section of CONSTITUTION.md no longer describes no-console-log
A new Evolution Log entry dated today records the removal with the stated reason
Running tests/governance/run.sh still exits 0 on the seeded repo after removal
The skill created exactly one new commit containing the removal with a conventional-commit subject
If the repo contains any references to the removed rule name (e.g., in a README or CI doc), the skill surfaced them to the user rather than silently leaving dangling references

evals.prompt: Can you run a governance health check and tell me if any of these rules look stale?
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes that this is a health-check request, not a targeted amendment. It does not edit files, does not stage changes, and answers directly.
assertions: No files under tests/governance/rules/ or CONSTITUTION.md were modified
The skill explicitly identified the request as a review/health-check rather than an amendment request
The skill answered directly without staging changes

evals.prompt: Add a rule called plan-captured. The goal is that every substantive change ships with an updated plan in plans/*.md so reviewers can see the intent, not just the diff.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats this as a change-set obligation, not a repo-state existence check. It creates or updates a rule that inspects the staged diff locally and the branch diff in CI so a substantive change without a companion plans/*.md update fails mechanically. The constitution entry says the rule blocks substantive changes landing without an updated plan, and the final summary explicitly names the bad merge, policy surface, and enforcement surface.
assertions: The final summary explicitly classifies the rule as a change-set obligation or equivalent wording
The new or updated rule check inspects changed files (for example via git diff --cached or a branch-diff fallback) rather than only checking whether plans/*.md exists
The rule check can fail when substantive files change without a companion plans/*.md update
The CONSTITUTION.md invariant for plan-captured describes the blocked bad merge in per-change terms, not just repo structure
The summary includes the chosen enforcement surface and why it fits
